clue.text: Knight breaks into a charge for monarch

indicators.note: something that breaks into another thing forces its way inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a charge is a price asked for something
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A mounted knight bursts in on a cavalry charge to reach the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks into' puts N inside PRICE: PRI-N-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal heir or ruler of a principality is a sovereign figure, a reasonable stand-in for a monarch.

clue.text: Trouble in Shanghai

definitions.meaning: to harass or urge someone insistently
to force a man into service at sea

explanation.surface: Someone reports difficulties in a Chinese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean coercing someone: badgering them, or seizing them for naval service as a press gang did.

clue.text: Reserved an attraction appearing in hotel

indicators.note: a performer appearing in a venue is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
a draw is something that attracts crowds

explanation.surface: A hotel offers a reserved booking that turns out to be a big attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drawn in on themselves is withdrawn and shy, the same as being reserved.

clue.text: Fighting under officer, more than one die showing timidity

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece written under another follows it

parts.note: CO is short for Commanding Officer
fighting on a national scale is war
dice is the plural of die

explanation.surface: A soldier fighting under his officer gambles with dice and shows fear.
explanation.walkthrough: CO, Commanding Officer, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is lack of courage, the state of showing timidity, though strictly a noun for that quality.

clue.text: Fleming tours corrupt African city

indicators.note: someone touring a place goes all round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: Ian Fleming was the author of the James Bond novels
corrupt means bad, rotten

explanation.surface: A novelist travels round a crooked city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming' points to the James Bond author by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria.

clue.text: Anger about gallons of water in the hull

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: bile is bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: A sailor fumes at the gallons of water swilling in the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty water collecting in a ship's lowest compartment is called by this name.

clue.text: Embassy official losing ten or's testimonial

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter comes off the word

parts.note: a diplomat is an official at an embassy
T stands for tenor, as in the SATB voice parts of a choir

explanation.surface: An embassy official loses a singer's letter of reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the T (tenor) off DIPLOMAT. T is the tenor line in choral SATB scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course is a formal testimonial of achievement.

clue.text: Visual problem for listeners in the dark

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, contained by it

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: Being able to hear in the dark compensates for poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia, seeing only close things clearly, is an eye condition, a sight problem.

clue.text: Tolerate drink that's a dis appointment

parts.note: to let something happen is to tolerate it
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Putting up with a drink that turns out a let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax that fails to meet expectations is a disappointment.

clue.text: Fielder gets practice in landing

parts.note: a slip is a close catching fielder in cricket
a way can mean a habit or customary practice

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder has some practice at catching on landing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand beside the wicketkeeper to catch edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp where boats are hauled out or launched is a kind of landing place.

clue.text: Winger in a last-minute switch

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, contained by it

parts.note: a late, as in a late change, is a last-minute one
a tern is a sea bird, something with wings

explanation.surface: A football winger comes on as a last-minute substitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TERN inside A LATE: AL-TERN-ATE. 'Winger' suggests football but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to swap back and forth, to switch between two things.

clue.text: Footwear for English banker wearing suit

indicators.note: a body wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: spades is a suit in a pack of cards, giving spade
a rill is a small stream, something with banks

explanation.surface: An English banker in a suit has picked unusual shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a stream or river, something with banks, not a person in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-soled canvas shoe is a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Expel saint after university

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: A saint is thrown out after his university days.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or remove someone from a position is to expel them.

clue.text: Scot is travelling west in the Middle East

indicators.note: in an across light, going west reads right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish first name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman heads west on a journey across the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run is read backwards, as an across light read westward runs right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of that name lies between Egypt and Israel, a region found in the Middle East; the definition describes its location.

clue.text: Marsupials briefly climbing over authorised professional

indicators.note: in a down light the reversed piece spreads over the other, enclosing it
in a down light climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: roos is a short form of kangaroos
licit means lawful, authorised

explanation.surface: Kangaroos clamber about over some qualified professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the reversed piece as SOOR, which then wraps the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who advises clients is a qualified professional.

clue.text: Alienate unruly sergeant

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An undisciplined sergeant drives people away.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them unfriendly, to drive them apart.

clue.text: Powerful, inscrutable detective found in river

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
Charlie Chan is a fictional detective known for his inscrutable manner

explanation.surface: A powerful, enigmatic detective is found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Trent flows through the English Midlands; Charlie Chan is a 1930s film detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is forceful and incisive, which is powerful.

clue.text: Poles arrest modern trollop

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
latter means more recent, modern

explanation.surface: Polish police arrest a modern woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' has the poles S and N holding LATTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a slovenly woman, an old-fashioned insult like trollop.

clue.text: Hit fellow in relationship

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or hit them
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man is struck by someone within a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry this is a ratio of opposite to adjacent sides, a mathematical relationship.

clue.text: Roget mistreated fungal disease

indicators.note: something mistreated is handled badly, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The thesaurus compiler was badly handled and caught a fungal disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungus infecting rye and other cereals, causing a plant disease.

clue.text: Foolishly enrage large soldier

indicators.note: acting foolishly means without sense, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big soldier is foolishly provoked into rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army officer of high rank is a soldier.

clue.text: I commit fraud to get religious portrait

parts.note: to con someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Someone forges a painting of a saint for money.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orthodox devotional painting of a saint is a religious portrait.

clue.text: Diagnostic tool is Tom's preserver

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a canner preserves food in tins

explanation.surface: A hospital scanner is described as belonging to someone named Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A computerised tomography machine produces body images for medical diagnosis.

clue.text: Many slim and lift weights

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
lean means slim

explanation.surface: Lots of people get thin by lifting weights.
explanation.walkthrough: In weightlifting the clean (as in clean and jerk) raises the bar to the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing a barbell from floor to shoulders in one move is a weightlifting term, so lifting weights.

clue.text: Fast runner in dash on first of December

indicators.note: in a down light a piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: elan is dash, flair

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A speedy athlete sprints at the start of December.
explanation.definitionFit: This antelope can run at speed across the African plains.

clue.text: Pete is ruined in eastern currency upturn

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, contained by it

parts.note: the sen is a coin of Japan and other Asian countries

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pete's finances are wrecked by a jump in an Asian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the name gives TEEP, which sits inside the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To steepen is to rise more sharply, to tilt upward, as a verb sense of upturn.

clue.text: Reasonable distance on the golf course

parts.note: fair means reasonable, just
way can mean distance, as in a long way

explanation.surface: A fair distance to cover on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The mown strip between tee and green is a part of a golf course; the definition locates it rather than naming it.

clue.text: Reprimand sailor

definitions.meaning: a naval seaman below officer rank

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling-off is a dressing-down, and a naval rank-and-file seaman also has this name.

clue.text: Uninspiring Tory leader enters firm

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: solid means firm

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dull Conservative leader joins a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives T; 'enters' puts it inside SOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is dull and impassive, unexciting, so uninspiring.
